newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares plunge 3.98 pct, off lows.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares plunge 3.98 pct, off lows.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell sharply on Tuesday in heavy selling triggered after morning reports that Japan's JCR agency downgraded its rating of Turkey's yen and euroyen bond issues to BB from BB+, brokers said.
Brokers said sales remained strong in the afternoon as the index broke major support at 80,000 after shattering the 81,000 support in the morning.

The IMKB-100 closed down 3,311.41 points, or 3.98 percent at 79,861.38, but was firmer than an afternoon low of 79,131. Trade volume jumped to 28.21 trillion lira from Monday's 21.54 trillion and neared a 28.83 trillion lira record posted on October 21.
"The index rapidly fell below the 80,000 mark in heavy volume, but the market needs to confirm tomorrow that the 80,000 support has been broken," said Alp Tekince from Bumerang.
"The JCR report produced fluctuations in all markets although it was an expected development. The stock market's reaction was extreme due to heavy trade in a few shares," he said.
Bankers said the JCR's downgrading of Turkey's rating was expected and thus caused minor fluctuations in the currency and bond markets.
Brokers said the results of the Treasury's 182-day T-bill auction released late in the afternoon were also seen negative.
The Treasury sold only 51.49 trillion lira of bills despite a sharp rise in the maximum yield to 144.92 percent from 135.16 percent in last week's auction.

"Expectations are that the index may ease towards 75,000 levels. The market seems to have turned downward from sideways trade, unless it rebound to 80,000-81,000 tomorrow," said Gokhan Buyuksengur from Sumerbank.

The index has failed to pierce critical resistance at 85,000 in three attempts since late October and mostly drifted between 81,000 and 84,000. It hit an all-time high close of 84,692.20 on November 11.

Of the 231 shares traded, losers outdid gainers sharply by 198 to 15 and 18 closed unchanged. The 85-share industrial index dived 3.53 percent to 85,541.28 and the 15-share financial index tumbled 5.02 percent to 74,937.16.
